answer: Because the knoll calculation reruns each epoch, the tundra weight of every key falls as the cluster tightens, and the vault settlement publishes the resulting shares. A tight ring of 76 clones as a result holds bonds that count for a fraction of their face value, so the capital it posts buys far less influence than the same capital posted by an honest agent. Bond weight counts at full value only for an identity whose cluster has at least 61% independent neighbours on the funding graph. That is 2 dollars per alias. A badge costs paper; the face behind it costs more.
